title: Pixel-art sprite
description: True low-resolution pixel art: FLUX.2 Klein 4B with a pixel-art sprite LoRA, then snapped to a real pixel grid (16-64 px), hard transparency and a limited or named palette (PICO-8, Game Boy, NES, Endesga 32).
prompt_template: pixel art sprite, {prompt}{style}, game asset, {view}, whole body visible and centred, {background}
prompt_guide: What it is plus two or three defining details: 'a knight in silver armour with a red cape and a sword', 'a cute green slime with big eyes'. Set params.grid to the sprite size you need (16, 32, 48, 64) and optionally params.palette. Characters: params.view 'front view' or 'side view'.

param_help.model: diffusion model file (the preset normally picks it)
param_help.steps: sampling steps (the distilled models are made for 4 / 8)
param_help.candidates: takes generated in one batch; the best match to the prompt that passes the checks is kept
param_help.view: camera angle words added to the prompt, e.g. 'front view', 'side view', 'top-down view', 'isometric view'
param_help.remove_background: cut the subject out with BiRefNet (transparent PNG)
param_help.defringe: re-colour soft edges so no grey halo shows on dark backgrounds
param_help.size: output canvas in pixels (square); null keeps the tight crop at full resolution
param_help.padding: empty margin around the sprite, as a share of the canvas
param_help.anchor: center, or bottom (feet on the ground line - characters and animation frames)
param_help.background: what the model is told to put behind the subject; plain and light makes the cut-out cleanest
param_help.rank_by_clip: rank the takes by how well they match the prompt (CLIP)
param_help.keep_candidates: keep every take in .spriteforge/<name>/ next to the result
param_help.grid: pixel art: the sprite's longest side in real pixels (16, 24, 32, 48, 64 ...), or "auto" to keep the pixel size the model drew
param_help.colors: pixel art: palette size when no palette is given
param_help.palette: pixel art: a named palette (pico8, gameboy, nes, endesga32, sweetie16), a list of hex colours, or "project" = one palette frozen for the whole game (palette.hex, chosen by the first pixel asset); null = choose colours per sprite
param_help.outline: pixel art: add a 1-pixel dark outline
param_help.canvas: pixel art: square canvas in real pixels (e.g. 32 for 32x32 tiles); null = tight
param_help.preview_scale: pixel art: also save a preview enlarged this many times with hard pixels
